articleTitle: The Impact of Standards on Maximo's Integration Capability
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on Enterprise Integration of Control Systems
abstract: Summary form only given. Maximo is the leading 'best of breed' asset and maintenance management system. As such there has been an evolution of a standards based approach to both ERP integration and plant floor integration over the past 10 years. This evolution has incorporated the development of standards and standards based organisations, the developments in service oriented architectures, as well as the changing demands and expectations of the user communities. In the future we should see these three aspects coming together to deliver a vision of low cost, flexible and seamless integration

articleTitle: ISA-95- Setting the Stage for Integration of MES and ICD Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on Enterprise Integration of Control Systems
abstract: This presentation describes the reasons for, and history of, the emergence of ISA-95, including how it relates to other enterprise integration standards such as ISA-88, ISA 99, and various ISO, IEC, and CEN standards. It sets the stage for the wide application of ISA-95 and describes additional standards which have evolved around it. Finally, it discusses how ISA-95 may be integrated with traditional project engineering and systems development methodologies, to provide an overall master planning approach for ICD (industrial control domain) and MES (manufacturing execution systems)

articleTitle: A Business Perspective on the Benefits of Real-Time Data Integration
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on Enterprise Integration of Control Systems
abstract: The presentation would identify the business drivers on UK manufacturing and identify the priorities for real time data integration. Demanding customers are requiring time compression of all aspects of the supply chain. Responsive operations are essential and a necessary but not sufficient condition for excellent real time supply chains. While manufacturing leaders rarely have an interface issue many #m's are wasted installing complex enterprise management processes around poor operations

articleTitle: Practical Application of ISA-S95 Enterprise/Control System Integration
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on Enterprise Integration of Control Systems
abstract: Globalization has translated into local business drivers of reducing costs, increasing production agility, reducing product change and roll-out times and maximizing asset effectiveness. These business drivers are requiring manufacturing organizations to perform at ever higher levels with fewer staff and at lower costs. A key response to these requirements being seen in all manufacturing segments is to more closely integrate manufacturing systems with enterprise resource planning and asset management systems. This presentation explains how open standards, such as ISA-S95, are being used to accomplish this integration with lower risk and shorter implementation times. It examines the outline definition within the S95 standard and explains how practical application of the standard can be achieved through defined business scenarios such as schedule management, batch reporting, real-time KPI alerting and optimized maintenance management

publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on Enterprise Integration of Control Systems
abstract: With ever-increasing competitiveness and globalization, innovative manufacturers are adapting and optimizing their methods to the 21st century "pull" markets. One of the biggest challenges of this is the integration of the various business systems. GE Fanuc are actively involved in the development and implementation of the ISA95 standards to address this area, integrating across the enterprise

articleTitle: S95: The Implications for Manufacturing Databases
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on Enterprise Integration of Control Systems
abstract: The presentation introduce the S95 standard and the implications for manufacturing database design. It covers the information exchange between the enterprise and control systems; what information, activities, resources and functions are involved and how they need to be organised and structured. The presentation concludes with the advantages of S95 including reductions in risks, errors and costs associated with enterprise-control system integration

articleTitle: The Business Case Approach to Manufacturing IT
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on Enterprise Integration of Control Systems
abstract: Many IT projects in manufacturing fail to really deliver the benefits for which they are capable, this is largely down to poor requirement definition, unclear business objectives or more importantly the right buy in across the business. This presentation explores how the issues facing manufacturing can be linked through tangible/intangible commercial measures, defining how improvement actions can be supported by the capabilities of MES

articleTitle: ERP Implementation and Maintenance in a Lean Environment (The Importance of People and Process)
publicationTitle: 2006 IET Seminar on Enterprise Integration of Control Systems
abstract: Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems were introduced into organisations to provide a fully integrated business solution (IBS) and maintain competitive advantage. However, many of these ERP implementations experienced cost and schedule overruns and loss of system functionality. The implementation process is known to be difficult, wasteful and typically costing five times the purchase price. This work aims to identify leading practice in ERP implementation and support through a literature review and interviewing process with 15 UK aerospace companies as part of the UK lean aerospace initiative and also seeks to examine the relationship and application of lean practices with ERP systems. Despite the better understanding developed by this research and the improved methods and tools provided by the vendors of ERP and other control systems since the research was completed the issues raised are still, in the authors view, relevant
